title: Learning to Notice the Seasons Again
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] People sometimes ask me why I care so much about small changes in the weather and the plants around my street.
Narrator: [gently] Honestly, I did not always notice these things. For years, one month felt the same as any other to me.
Narrator: [reflective] Then last year, I started keeping a small notebook, just to write one line each day about the sky, the air, or something growing nearby.
Narrator: [calm] At first, I wrote simple things, like today it rained, or today the wind was strong and the leaves fell early.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Slowly, I began noticing patterns I had never seen before, even though they happened every single year of my life.
Narrator: [warmly] I noticed the wind changes direction before the rainy season starts, days before the first big storm actually arrives.
Narrator: [gently] I noticed certain flowers bloom for only two short weeks, and then disappear completely until the following year.
Narrator: [honestly] I used to feel like the seasons were background noise, something happening while I focused on more important things.
Narrator: [reflective] Now I see them differently, as a quiet, careful rhythm that continues whether I am paying attention or not.
Narrator: [with hope] Writing this small notebook made me slower in a good way. I started walking to work instead of driving, just to notice more.
Narrator: [gently] It is such a small habit, only a few minutes each evening, but it changed how connected I feel to the world outside my window.
Narrator: [peacefully] I no longer feel like a stranger passing through my own neighborhood. I feel like someone who actually knows this place.
Narrator: [warmly] Maybe you walk past the same trees and skies every day without truly seeing them. I hope you find your own small notebook too.
